title: Edge cluster assembly notes and runbook (bare-metal + vSphere)
content:
PURPOSE:
Quick, usable set of notes and a lightweight runbook for assembling on-prem K8s clusters at the edge or colo. Covers both bare-metal PXE/I PXE flows and vSphere VM template flows, terraform module patterns we are trying, and a cautious upgrade plan for control plane and workers. This is intentionally a working cheatsheet — copy into a formal runbook when stabilized.

SCOPE / ASSUMPTIONS:
- Target clusters: small (3-7 control-plane), medium (3 control-plane + autoscaling workers), and edge single rack clusters.
- Networking: VLAN per-tenant, BGP for pod egress in larger sites, native L2 for small edge sites.
- Inventory and secrets: hardware inventory in asset-db, secrets in Vault or customer KMS.
- Image sources: internal registry for k8s images; vSphere template built from a minimal golden-image build pipeline.

DECISION MATRIX (choose approach)
- Bare-metal if you need direct host access, NIC passthrough, or faster inference with GPU PCIe. Use iPXE + ignition/ignition-like config.
- vSphere if customer already has VMware and wants lifecycle via templates, snapshots. Use terraform-provider-vsphere + cloud-init.
- Hybrid: control plane on vSphere (stable), workers on bare metal (GPU).

PRE-FLIGHT CHECKLIST (must be green before bootstrap)
- Hardware: IPMI reachable, BIOS settings (VT-d, SR-IOV if needed) verified.
- Networking: DHCP scope for bootstrap network reserved; OOB mgmt VLAN segregated; DNS entries for control plane FQDNs.
- Time: NTP configured (chrony) and reachable from all hosts.
- Storage: LVM/LocalPV nodes validated, or CSI drivers tested for SAN/NAS.
- BMC/RM: IPMI/vSphere credentials in Vault; service account with limited perms.
- Image: Golden OS image SHA256 verified, cloud-init templates available for vSphere.

PROVISIONING PATTERNS (notes + terraform module ideas)
- Modules: module.hosts (baremetal), module.vsphere-vm, module.networking, module.k8s-bootstrap. Keep modules small and idempotent.
- module.hosts variables: asset_id list, bmc_endpoint map, desired_hostname pattern, node_role (control, worker, infra).
- module.k8s-bootstrap outputs: kubeconfig_base64, control_plane_ips, bootstrap_token (rotate post-install).
- Lifecycle hooks: allow pre_provision and post_provision hooks (scripts stored in git repo, run via runner).
- State: remote state per-site (GCS/S3) to avoid cross-site interference.
- Secrets: do not store kubeadm tokens in TF state; inject from Vault at apply-time using transient provider.

Bare-metal sketch (high level)
1) reserve bootstrap network + DHCP scope
2) ensure iPXE server reachable, config templates staged (use rack-specific mac->profile mapping)
3) boot hosts into installer image which pulls ignition or cloud-init from signed URL
4) installer registers to asset-db, tags node-role
5) run terraform apply for module.k8s-bootstrap which calls kubeadm via remote-exec (or better: call a bootstrap controller image)
6) join workers with kubeadm join (token injected from Vault)

vSphere sketch (high level)
1) build VM template (minimal OS + cloud-init) via CI pipeline, store template name in terraform vars
2) terraform-provider-vsphere creates VMs from template, injects cloud-init user-data (kubeadm bootstrap script)
3) wait for node registration; labeling by metadata tag
4) use vSphere snapshot strategy before upgrades

Kubeadm vs Cluster API discussion (short)
- kubeadm: simple, fewer moving parts, better for controlled onprem installs. Good for small clusters.
- Cluster API (CAPI): better for declarative lifecycle and for vSphere heavy shops; more complex.
- Recommendation: start with kubeadm for edge pilots, evaluate CAPI for multi-site scale.

UPGRADE PLAN (control plane + workers)
- Principle: keep control plane quorum and node-level PDBs in mind. Always have a tested rollback path (snapshot + etcd backup).
- Control plane (kubeadm):
  * Pre-checks: control-plane nodes CPU/mem, etcd health, no outstanding upgrades in progress.
  * Step 0: etcd snapshot (off-cluster storage and validate restore)
  * Step 1: upgrade kubelet on one control plane node, drain with --ignore-daemonsets, --delete-local-data as appropriate
  * Step 2: run kubeadm upgrade apply <target> on that control-plane node
  * Step 3: wait for apiserver, controller-manager, scheduler to be Ready then proceed to next control-plane node
  * Note: for 3-node control plane, do one node at a time. For 5+, still one at a time but watch quorum.
- Worker nodes:
  * Batch size: default 10-20% of workers (configurable) or max N nodes in a rack to avoid cross-rack impact
  * Use RollingUpdate with node drain; validate important inference pods restart within expected time

Backups and disaster recovery
- etcd: scheduled snapshots to object store + verified restores run monthly in staging
- PVs: document RPO for customers; snapshot-based restores for CSI drivers (check driver compatibility)
- Control plane: vSphere snapshot before major upgrades (but don't rely solely on snapshots for etcd)

Operational run commands (quick cheats)
- check etcd health: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 endpoint status --cacert=... --cert=... --key=...
- drain a node safely: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=30m
- kubeadm token create --print-join-command (rotate after use)

Common failure modes and mitigations (collected)
- DHCP scope exhaustion on bootstrap net -> pre-reserve / smaller lease times during bootstrap OR use per-rack DHCP pools
- Missing BMC creds in Vault -> fail early check and alert automation team
- Slow image download on edge site -> pre-cache images on local registry node (pull-through cache)
- vSphere disk provisioning slow -> increase template CPU to speed cloud-init; use guestinfo to pass minimal userdata and run heavy work from internal registry

Security notes
- Kubeconfig: limited-time service users for bootstrap; revoke after join to avoid long-lived tokens in TF state.
- Access: separate management VLAN for admin access; restrict API server loadbalancer to management IPs unless customer requires public access.
- Secrets: always reference secrets via Vault/KMS; do not embed plaintext tokens in git.

Open questions / TODOs (action items)
- Decide default: kubeadm or CAPI for v1.30+ clusters (engineering + research to prototype CAPI for vSphere by end Q1).
- Terraform module: implement a preflight validation step (terraform plan output parser) — Marco to prototype.
- gpu-node boot speed: Jia to trial u-boot vs ipmitool serial over LAN for faster retries.
- Add automated smoke tests post-bootstrap (kube-bench minimal + inference sample) — create MR to integrate into pipeline.

Notes on documentation hygiene
- This doc is quick notes. When approach stabilizes, move to: confluence: /display/OPS/Onprem+Runbooks and create a runbook per site type with checklists and operator scripts.

Appendix: useful links & commands
- vault read secret/platform/bmc-creds/<site>
- terraform apply -var-file=site-vars.tfvars modules/edge-cluster --target=module.hosts
- gitlab pipeline: infra/templates/build-golden-image (artifact: vm-template-2024-09-xx)

END - ping authors for clarifications.
